name: Losar at Zang Dhok Palri and the Tibetan monasteries
when: February or early March (first day of the Tibetan lunar year)
summary: Losar is the Tibetan New Year, celebrated in Kalimpong by Tibetan and Bhutia families and at monasteries such as Zang Dhok Palri on Durpin Hill. Expect prayers, butter lamps, prayer flags and family feasts over several days.
body: Losar marks the first day of the Tibetan lunar calendar, so its date moves each year, usually falling in February and sometimes in early March. In the days before, families clean their homes and make khapse, fried biscuits in twisted shapes. Monks hold rituals to clear away the obstacles of the old year.

On the day itself, people visit monasteries to light butter lamps, offer khada scarves and hang new prayer flags. Zang Dhok Palri on Durpin Hill and the older Tibetan monasteries in town are the main places to see this. Some monasteries hold masked dances in the period around Losar, but the schedule varies, so ask at the monastery.

For travellers, Losar is a quiet, respectful festival rather than a show. Shops run by Tibetan families may close for two or three days. Visitors are usually welcome at monasteries during the day if they dress modestly and follow the monks' lead.
tips: Check the Losar date for the year, which follows the Tibetan calendar
Walk clockwise around stupas and prayer wheels
Ask before photographing rituals or monks
Expect some Tibetan-run shops and restaurants to close for a few days
Carry warm clothes; February mornings on Durpin Hill are cold

faqs.a: Losar falls on the first day of the first month of the Tibetan lunar calendar, which usually lands in February and sometimes in early March. The exact date changes every year, and Bhutanese and Sikkimese calendars can differ by a day or so. Check the date with a monastery or a Tibetan calendar before planning around it.

faqs.q: Can tourists attend Losar prayers at Durpin monastery?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Visitors can enter Zang Dhok Palri and other monasteries during daytime prayers if they dress modestly, remove shoes before entering halls and keep quiet. Do not sit on raised seats or point your feet at the altar. Photography inside prayer halls is often not allowed, so ask first.

faqs.q: Are there masked dances at Losar in Kalimpong?
faqs.a: Some Tibetan Buddhist monasteries hold cham, or masked dances, around the New Year, but the dates and places vary from year to year and some dances happen before Losar rather than on it. Ask at Zang Dhok Palri or your hotel a few days ahead. Do not plan a trip only around a dance you have not confirmed.

faqs.q: What should I eat during Losar?
faqs.a: Look for khapse, the fried twisted biscuits made in Tibetan homes before the New Year, and guthuk, a noodle soup eaten on the eve of Losar in many families. Tibetan restaurants in Kalimpong may serve special dishes, though some close for family celebrations. Butter tea is offered in homes and is polite to accept.

name: Dashain and Tihar in Kalimpong
when: Late September to November (Dashain in Ashwin, Tihar about three weeks later)
summary: Dashain and Tihar are the biggest festivals of Kalimpong's Nepali-speaking majority. Dashain brings red tika and family blessings; Tihar brings oil lamps, marigold garlands and evening songs from house to house.
body: Dashain is a fifteen-day festival that ends on Vijaya Dashami, the same day as Bengal's Durga Puja ends. On that day elders put red tika and jamara, young barley shoots, on the foreheads of younger relatives and give blessings. Families travel home, so jeeps and buses are full before and after the main days.

Tihar follows about three weeks later and lasts five days. People honour crows, dogs and cows on successive days, decorate houses with marigolds and oil lamps for Laxmi Puja, and finish with Bhai Tika, when sisters bless their brothers. Groups of young people go from house to house singing deusi and bhailo songs.

For visitors, these weeks bring lit-up houses, swings in some villages and a festive mood in the bazaar. They also bring peak season. October rooms and cars sell out early, and some shops close on the main tika days.
tips: Book stays and cars at least two months ahead for October
Expect shared jeeps to be packed around Vijaya Dashami
Keep small notes for deusi and bhailo singers who visit homestays
Village homestays are a good way to see the festival from inside a family
Check exact dates, which follow the lunar calendar

faqs.q: When are Dashain and Tihar celebrated?
faqs.a: Dashain falls in the lunar month of Ashwin, usually in late September or October, ending on Vijaya Dashami. Tihar comes about three weeks later, around the time of Diwali, in October or November. Dates change each year with the lunar calendar, so check them before booking a trip around the festivals.

faqs.q: Is October a good time to visit Kalimpong despite the festivals?
faqs.a: Yes, it is one of the best months for weather and views, and the festivals add colour. The cost is crowding: rooms and cars are booked by holidaymakers from Kolkata and Siliguri, and prices rise. Book two months ahead, avoid travelling on the main tika days, and expect some shops to close.

faqs.q: Can visitors take part in Dashain or Tihar?
faqs.a: Homestay hosts often invite guests to watch the tika or the Laxmi Puja lamps, and sometimes to receive a tika themselves. Accept politely if you are comfortable, and follow your host's lead. During Tihar, groups of deusi and bhailo singers may sing at your homestay; it is usual to give them a small gift of money.

faqs.q: Do shops and transport close during Dashain?
faqs.a: On the main tika days many shops and offices close, and some drivers take leave to be with family. Shared jeeps run but fill fast before and after the holiday. Arrange your car in advance and keep cash, since some ATMs run dry. Check current status before you travel.

name: Gaeboo Achyuk birthday at Damsang Fort
summary: On 20 December, Lepchas from Kalimpong, Darjeeling and Sikkim gather at the ruins of Damsang Fort near Pedong to mark the birthday of Gaeboo Achyuk, the last Lepcha king of the area. It is a community event with prayers, rituals and cultural programmes.
body: Gaeboo Achyuk, also written Gyalpo Ajok, ruled the Lepcha kingdom of Damsang in the late seventeenth century. Local tradition says he built the fort at Damsang to hold off the Bhutanese, who later captured and executed him. After that the Kalimpong area came under Bhutanese rule until the British annexed it in 1865.

Each year on 20 December Lepcha associations hold a gathering at the fort ruins between Pedong and Algarah. There are prayers led by Lepcha priests, speeches on Lepcha history and language, songs and dances in traditional dress. It is one of the few times the Lepcha story of these hills is told in public, on the ground where it happened.

This is a community observance, not a tourist festival. Visitors who come quietly are welcome, but there are few facilities, and the road to the fort is rough. Sillery Gaon, a short drive away, is the most comfortable base.
tips: Stay in Sillery Gaon or Pedong the night before
Dress warmly; late December mornings are cold on the ridge
Ask before photographing rituals and elders
Carry water and snacks, since stalls are few
Confirm the programme with your homestay host, as arrangements vary

faqs.a: Gaeboo Achyuk, also written Gyalpo Ajok, was a Lepcha chieftain who ruled from Damsang in the late seventeenth century. Allied with Tibet, he fought Bhutan for control of these hills. Accounts say the Bhutanese captured and executed him, after which the Kalimpong area came under Bhutan until 1865. Lepchas remember him as their last king here.

The ruins lie on a ridge between Pedong and Algarah in Kalimpong district, roughly 6 km from Icche Gaon and a short drive from Sillery Gaon. Only parts of the stone walls survive among the trees. The last stretch is a rough road and a short walk, so wear sturdy shoes.

faqs.q: Can tourists attend the 20 December gathering?
faqs.a: Yes, quiet and respectful visitors are generally welcome. It is a Lepcha community event, so follow the lead of organisers, stay out of the way of rituals and ask before taking photographs. There are no tickets. Your homestay host in Sillery Gaon or Pedong can tell you the timing for the year.

faqs.q: Is late December a good time to visit Sillery Gaon?
faqs.a: Yes, December is usually clear, with good views of Kanchenjunga from Sillery Gaon and Ramitey Dara. Nights drop to a few degrees above freezing, so bring warm layers. Christmas and New Year week is busy with weekenders, so book homestays early if your trip runs past 20 December.
